I go to the office every morning.
I get up at seven in the morning.
시 hours take native numbers: 일곱 시 (ilgop si = 7 o'clock).
I leave the house at eight.
나가요 (nagayo) = go out: 집에서 나가요 = leave the house.
I commute to work by subway.
출근해요 (chulgeunhaeyo) = go to work; (으)로 = by: 지하철로 = by subway.
I transfer from the bus to the subway.
It takes forty minutes to the office.
분 minutes take Sino numbers: 사십 분 (sasip bun = 40 minutes).
There are so many people on the morning subway.
I missed the bus this morning.
놓쳤어요 (nochyeosseoyo) = missed it — buses, trains, chances.
So I was a little late to work.
그래서 (geuraeseo) = so/therefore — links a cause to a result.
I wait for the bus at the stop.
I walk ten minutes to the subway station.
I listen to music on the subway.
The traffic is really bad today.
길이 막혀요 (giri makyeoyo) = 'the road is blocked' — Korean for a traffic jam.
What time do you go to work?
I get to work by nine.
까지 (kkaji) = by/until: 아홉 시까지 (ahop sikkaji = by 9 o'clock).
The office is close to my house.
The roads are crowded at rush hour.
퇴근 시간 (toegeun sigan) = 'leaving-work time' = the evening rush hour.
Yesterday I came home by taxi.
From next week I'll bike to work.
부터 (buteo) = from/starting: 다음 주부터 = from next week.
I buy coffee on the way to work.
출근길 (chulgeungil) = the way to work; -길 (gil) makes 'route' words.
I read the news on the subway.
There's a cafe in front of the office.
전에 (jeone) = before: 출근 전에 (chulgeun jeone = before work).
우리 (uri) = our — Koreans say 'our company,' 'our family,' even 'our house.'
At work use title + 님: 과장님 (gwajangnim = manager) — never the bare name!
The department head is on a business trip now.
부장님 (bujangnim) = department head; 중이에요 (jungieyo) = in the middle of.
I had lunch with the team leader.
팀장님 (timjangnim) = team leader — 팀 (tim) comes from English 'team.'
The boss is in a meeting right now.
-세요 adds respect for the boss: 회의 중이세요 (hoeui jungiseyo = is in a meeting).
A new colleague is coming next week.
I work on the marketing team.
안 돼요 (an dwaeyo) = it doesn't work — an everyday essential phrase.
I check my email in the morning.
I sent the report to the department head.
한테 (hante) = to a person: 부장님한테 = to the department head.
I put the documents on the desk.
위에 (wie) = on top of: 책상 위에 (chaeksang wie = on the desk).
My colleague isn't at her desk today.
자리 (jari) = seat/desk — 자리에 없어요 = away from their desk.
I eat lunch at the company cafeteria.
I drink coffee with a colleague.
랑 (rang) = with/and, casual: 동료랑 (dongnyorang = with a colleague).
There's even more work in the afternoon.
아직 (ajik) = yet/still: 아직 안 끝났어요 = not done yet.
I have so much to do today.
할 일 (hal il) = things to do — 할 turns 하다 into 'to-do.'
On Friday afternoons I feel good.
기분이 좋아요 (gibuni joayo) = 'my mood is good' = I feel great.
힘들어요 (himdeureoyo) = it's tough — for effort and energy, not taste.
다녀요 (danyeoyo) = go regularly — Korean's verb for attending work or school.
My older sister works at the same company too.
I'm getting a lot of stress these days.
스트레스를 받아요 (seuteureseureul badayo) = 'receive stress' = to be stressed.
-실 (sil) = room: 회의실 (hoeuisil) = meeting room, 화장실 = bathroom.
There's an important presentation next week.
잘 (jal) = well: 잘 끝났어요 = it ended well.
I got a lot of questions at the meeting.
